Costs (Kosten) – step-by-step workflow

For Kretoss · 16 November 2026 · version 3

This document answers your question 4: the workflow for adding expenses, proposing budgets, approvals, settling up and payments. Kosten has two tabs: Uitgaven (costs already made) and Nog nodig (things that still need to be bought, with a budget agreed in advance). Sketches of every screen are at the end, translated into English and all in the final style (A6) with the new child colours: build them like this. Colours, cards and fonts are in Stijlgids v1.2. Everything in this document is decided.

About your suggestion to split everything equally: please do not build a fixed 50/50. Parents set their own fixed split once (for example 60/40). For each expense they can still choose 50/50 or "fully my own" instead.

App texts: Dutch and English

The app is in Dutch. The sketches at the end show the English translation, so you can follow them. In the app, use the Dutch texts. In this document the Dutch app text is in bold; this table gives the English meaning.

Rules that drive everything

  • Paid from the joint child account (Kindrekening): never settled. It is shown in the overview only.
  • Paid from your own account: settled with the chosen split, but only for what the other parent agreed to.
  • Above the threshold (grensbedrag): always a budget proposal first – also when paying from the child account.
  • No agreement at all: the expense is fully for the parent's own account and is never settled.

Setup, once (sketch 1)

Step 1 – How the parents handle costs

  1. A parent opens Kosten for the first time and chooses one of two ways:
    1. Via alimentatie en kindrekening – nothing is settled. The balance of the child account is kept outside the app; the app does not track it.
    2. Extra kosten samen delen – extra costs are shared; the app calculates who owes whom.
  2. The other parent gets a request to confirm. The screen says: "Staat er in jullie ouderschapsplan of convenant iets anders, dan geldt dat."

Step 2 – Fixed split

  1. Parents set a fixed split, for example Jij 60% · Joris 40%. Quick choices: 50/50, 60/40, 70/30, Anders (custom).
  2. This split is the default for every expense. Per expense the parent can also choose 50/50 or Helemaal voor mij (fully my own, not settled).

Step 3 – Approval threshold (grensbedrag)

  1. Parents agree on an amount, for example € 50.
  2. Up to that amount a parent may buy something without approval in advance.
  3. Above that amount there must always first be a budget proposal that the other parent approves (steps 5 and 6). This also applies to the child account.

Steps 1 to 3 are saved together and sent to the other parent with Opslaan en aan [naam] voorleggen.

Expenses up to the threshold (sketch 2)

Step 4 – Add an expense

  1. Kosten → Uitgave toevoegen.
  2. Fields: amount, what for, for which child (one, more or all), receipt photo (optional up to the threshold).
  3. Waarmee heb je betaald? – Kindrekening or Mijn eigen rekening. This choice must be big and clear.
  4. Kindrekening → saved; the other parent sees it in the overview; nothing is settled.
  5. Own account → Hoe verdelen? – Jullie verdeling (default), 50/50 or Helemaal voor mij. The app shows the other parent's share, for example "Deel van Joris: € 16,00".
  6. Helemaal voor mij → saved, nothing is settled.
  7. Otherwise the other parent gets a request to confirm (step 9).

Expenses above the threshold (sketches 3 to 7)

Step 5 – Budget proposal (sketch 3)

  1. Fields: what for, for which child, budget amount, split (same three choices as step 4), optional note.
  2. The app shows the other parent's maximum share, for example "max. € 32,00".
  3. Voorstel versturen → the other parent gets the proposal. Status: Wacht op reactie.

Step 6 – The other parent decides (sketch 4)

  1. The other parent sees: what for, child, note, budget, split and their own share.
  2. Three buttons: Akkoord, Ander voorstel and Niet akkoord.
  3. Akkoord → the budget is approved; the parent can buy it.
  4. Ander voorstel → see step 7.
  5. Niet akkoord → the budget is rejected. If the parent still buys it, it is fully for their own account and is never settled.

Step 7 – Another proposal (Ander voorstel) (sketch 5)

  1. The other parent sees the original proposal and enters their own amount and/or split, with an optional note.
  2. Voorstel versturen → the first parent gets it and decides in the same way: Akkoord, Ander voorstel or Niet akkoord.
  3. Ends in Akkoord → that amount and split are the approved budget.
  4. Ends in Niet akkoord → no budget; the expense is fully for the parent's own account and is never settled.

Step 8 – Add the expense with the approved budget (sketches 6 and 7)

  1. When the amount is above the threshold, the expense screen asks: Bij welk budget hoort dit? and lists the approved budgets ("Akkoord van Joris op 12 nov").
  2. The parent picks the budget. The split comes from the budget.
  3. Receipt photo is required above the threshold.
  4. Amount within the budget → the expense goes directly to Nog te verrekenen. No extra confirmation is needed.
  5. Amount above the budget → see step 16.
  6. No approved budget → the app shows "Eerst een budgetvoorstel" with the button Budgetvoorstel doen (sketch 7). This also applies when paying from the child account. If the other parent does not agree, the expense is fully for the parent's own account.

Confirmation and overview (sketches 8 and 9)

Step 9 – The other parent confirms an expense up to the threshold (sketch 8)

  1. Only for own-account expenses up to the threshold (expenses with an approved budget skip this step).
  2. The other parent sees: what for, child, who paid from which account, total, split, their share and the receipt photo if added.
  3. Three buttons: Bevestigen, Ander voorstel and Niet akkoord.
  4. Bevestigen → the expense counts in "Nog te verrekenen".
  5. Ander voorstel → the other parent proposes a different amount or split; the first parent decides as in step 7.
  6. Niet akkoord → the expense is fully for the parent's own account and is never settled.

Step 10 – The Kosten page (sketch 9)

  1. Tabs Uitgaven and Nog nodig.
  2. Top block Nog te verrekenen: who pays whom and the amount ("Joris betaalt jou € 40,00"), the button Verrekenen, and in small text the agreement ("Jullie afspraak: jij 60% · Joris 40% · grens € 50") with Wijzigen. Only own-account expenses the other parent agreed to count.
  3. The + at the top right opens a sheet "Wat wil je toevoegen?" with Uitgave, Budget voorstellen and Iets voor Nog nodig (sketch 15). The same pattern as the + in the agenda.
  4. List of expenses with: child, date, who paid, label Kindrekening or Eigen rekening, and the status: Niet verrekenen, Wacht op [naam] (not counted yet), Bevestigd or Binnen budget · deel [naam] € ….
  5. A Wacht op jou block above the list shows proposals and confirmations the parent still has to answer, with one button.
  6. Parents who chose Via alimentatie en kindrekening see on top only what was spent together this month, without Verrekenen (sketch 16).

Settling up (sketch 10)

Step 11 – Verrekenen

  1. Top: the net amount and direction, for example Joris betaalt Sanne € 40,00, and the number of expenses.
  2. Below: Wat er verrekend wordt – one box per expense with: what for, child, Gekocht door [naam], account and split, total, share of each parent, and who pays whom for this expense.
  3. Below the list: Optelling – what each parent owes the other, and the net amount.
  4. Button Betaalverzoek sturen aan [naam]: no payment inside the app. The other parent gets a payment request with the amount, the description and the IBAN of the receiving parent (with copy buttons) and pays in their own bank app. If you can create an iDEAL payment link without a payment contract on our side, tell us; otherwise IBAN + copy buttons is fine.
  5. The receiving parent taps Ontvangen when the money is in. Button Al betaald buiten de app does the same for payments made another way.
  6. Then the expenses are marked Verrekend and the total goes back to € 0.

Nog nodig: things still to buy (sketches 11 to 14)

The tab Nog nodig is for things the children still need. A budget can always be agreed before anything is bought. When the item is bought, the costs are added from this tab.

Step 12 – The Nog nodig list (sketch 11)

  1. Every item shows: what, for which child, who buys it (a parent, or "nog niet afgesproken wie"), and its budget status.
  2. Budget status per item: Budget voorstellen (no budget yet), Budget € … · wacht op [naam], or Budget € … · akkoord van [naam].
  3. Below the list: Iets toevoegen and Eerder gekocht.

Step 13 – Add an item, with a budget proposal (sketch 12)

  1. Fields: what, for which child, who buys it (Ik / the other parent / Nog niet afgesproken).
  2. A budget proposal can always be made here: amount and split (same three choices as step 4). The other parent decides as in steps 6 and 7.
  3. A budget can also be proposed later from the item in the list.

Step 14 – Bought: add the costs from the item (sketch 13)

  1. On the item: Gekocht opens the cost screen, pre-filled with what, child, budget and split.
  2. The parent enters the actual amount, chooses Kindrekening or Mijn eigen rekening, and adds the receipt photo (required above the threshold).
  3. Kosten toevoegen creates the expense.

Step 15 – What happens next

  1. The item disappears from Nog nodig and moves to Eerder gekocht.
  2. Paid from the child account → nothing is settled.
  3. Paid from an own account, within the budget → the other parent's share goes directly to Nog te verrekenen.

Step 16 – More than the budget (sketch 14)

Applies to every expense with a budget, also from Nog nodig.

  1. The app shows how much it is above the budget, for example "€ 15 boven het budget".
  2. The other parent gets the question whether they approve the difference.
  3. Approved → the full amount is settled with the split.
  4. Not approved → only the approved budget is settled; the rest is for the parent who bought it.
  5. From Nog nodig the item disappears from the list in both cases and goes to Nog te verrekenen.

Statuses

Object Statuses
Expense Opgeslagen (kindrekening or fully own) · Wacht op bevestiging · Ander voorstel · Bevestigd · Binnen budget · Verschil wacht op akkoord · Niet akkoord (fully own account) · Verrekend
Budget proposal Wacht op reactie · Ander voorstel · Akkoord · Niet akkoord
Nog nodig item Nog nodig · Gekocht (moves to Eerder gekocht)

Show statuses as icon + word, never red or orange.

Data

  • Cost settings (per family): mode (1 = via alimentatie en kindrekening, 2 = extra kosten samen delen), split_parent_a, split_parent_b, approval_threshold, confirmed_by, confirmed_at.
  • Expense: id, amount, description, child_ids[], date, paid_by, paid_from (kindrekening / eigen), split_type (vast / 50_50 / eigen), share_a, share_b, budget_id, over_budget_amount, over_budget_approved, receipt_photo (required above the threshold), status, confirmed_by, confirmed_at, settlement_id.
  • Budget proposal: id, description, child_ids[], amount, split_type, note, status, proposed_by, decided_by, decided_at, counter_of (id of the proposal it answers).
  • Nog nodig item: id, description, child_ids[], buyer (parent / not agreed), budget_id, status, expense_id, bought_at.
  • Settlement: id, from_parent, to_parent, amount, expense_ids[], status (verzocht / ontvangen), requested_at, received_at.

Decided since the first version

  1. Betalen: a payment request that the parent pays in their own bank app, not a real payment inside the app (step 11).
  2. "Ander voorstel" is the word for every counter-proposal in the whole app, also in Kosten. Do not use "Ander voorstel".
  3. Look and feel: all sketches are in style A6 (soft gradient background, glass cards, child colours from the Kinderen page). Follow Stijlgids v1.2 for exact colours and sizes. Never use red or orange for a status.
